title: Airbyte 2.2: What to Know About the New Release
summary: Explore Airbyte 2.2, including its latest features, improvements, and key updates for building more reliable and efficient data pipelines.
body_markdown:
[Airbyte 2.2](https://docs.airbyte.com/release_notes/self-managed/v-2.2) shipped for self-managed instances on August 10 and it has some major Helm upgrades for you to keep in mind. You'll also notice security bug fixes and a job history optimization.


Check out the major highlights of this release before you upgrade to get the most out of the new version and avoid some obvious pitfalls.


If you still use Self-Managed Enterprise, do not upgrade. Speak to your Airbyte representative about switching to one of Airbyte's Cloud plans, which always have the latest capabilities and security improvements. Private Link is available if you require it.


## 1. Airbyte 2.2 improves enforcement of Helm chart V2 global defaults


As of Airbyte 2.1, you can only use Helm chart V2, which ignored` global.jobs.resources` . If you set a CPU or memory limit for sync jobs there, the chart ignored those limits and ran on defaults. Plenty of operators never noticed because a silently ignored limit acts like a generous limit.


In 2.2.0 those values take effect as fallbacks for the following keys:


- ` JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT`
- ` JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_REQUEST`
- ` JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT`
- ` JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST`


Keep in mind that keys scoped under` global.workloads.resources.mainContainer` take precedence; anything you leave unset falls back to the legacy value.


The same reactivation applies to` global.workloads.resources.replication.*` , which now sizes the replication orchestrator appropriately. You'll need to check the following values:


- ` REPLICATION_ORCHESTRATOR_CPU_LIMIT`
- ` REPLICATION_ORCHESTRATOR_CPU_REQUEST`
- ` REPLICATION_ORCHESTRATOR_MEMORY_LIMIT`
- ` REPLICATION_ORCHESTRATOR_MEMORY_REQUEST`


This separation helps you control the orchestrator and main container independently to account for their different workloads and appetites.


Take stock of these limits before you upgrade. A harmless value in 2.1.x can easily become a scheduling constraint on the first post-upgrade sync. If you tuned around the broken behavior by adding limits somewhere else, that limit will compound.


## 2. The Helm chart renders cleanly through your deployment tooling


If you pipe` helm template` output into Kustomize, or run any GitOps flow that renders manifests before applying them, 2.2 offers a couple of fixes.


The chart no longer emits duplicate` DATAPLANE_CLIENT_ID_SECRET_KEY` or` DATAPLANE_CLIENT_SECRET_SECRET_KEY` , and the Temporal UI deployment's resource and security context blocks are indented correctly. Kustomize will outright refuse duplicate keys and bad indentation, so this can take your work from a YAML with script patches all the way to a working pipeline.


Both the main chart and the data plane chart now accept a top-level` namespaceOverride` .` namespaceOverride` controls the namespace for two things:


- Chart-generated resources
- Internal service discovery


Rendered manifests always carry an explicit` metadata.namespace` set to` namespaceOverride` if configured, or the release namespace otherwise. That manifest namespace takes precedence over a` kubectl -n` call, so render your templates with a` --namespace` that matches the namespace you're deploying into.


## 3. HTTP Basic is no longer accepted


In self-managed Airbyte 2.2, any script, cron job, or CI step that calls the API with` curl -u` will break after the upgrade.


Instead, you'll need to request an access token from` /api/v1/applications/token` using` instance-admin-client-id` and` instance-admin-client-secret` . There may be more calls using HTTP Basic auth than you'd expect because it's an easy health check.


Two related fixes to note. Unauthenticated requests no longer advertise a Basic authentication challenge, which caused browsers to surface a native username and password dialog for anyone who hit the URL.


The server now also strips client-supplied internal authentication headers from incoming requests before deriving the trusted workspace and organization identity headers for authorization. This means Airbyte is less likely to accept a spoofed request.


The same updates apply to administrative invitation endpoints. Responses from` /v1/user_invitations/create` ,` /v1/user_invitations/list_pending` , and` /v1/user_invitations/cancel` no longer include` inviteCode` , so listing pending invitations doesn't include working invitation codes.` cancel` still accepts` inviteCode` as input.


## 4. No more false reporting on sync failures


Five of the fixes in this release share a similar theme. The sync was fine and the platform either reported a failure or destroyed the working state on the way out.


A sync that produces zero records used to fail. The container orchestrator could terminate a destination before the destination had a chance to shut down gracefully, and it missed exit-code files created through an atomic rename. Destinations now get up to 60 seconds to exit on their own before Airbyte stops them, and empty syncs complete normally. If you run incremental syncs on slow-moving tables, you should see fewer false alarms.


For connections on the socket transport, the workload launcher read CPU limits expressed in millicores as whole cores. A limit of` 500m` was read as 500 cores, and the computed socket count inflated enormously. That's now parsed correctly.


There's a big OAuth fix in this release. When a source emits a` CONTROL` message with refreshed OAuth configuration, Airbyte now saves the information earlier in the process. Before, cancelling or aborting a sync after the connector refreshed its token resulted in a lost rotated refresh token.


Two changes push errors to surface immediately. If Airbyte creates an attempt on a job that's already running or finished, the call returns a` 409 Conflict` so the workflow fails fast instead of retrying. Additionally, secret storage configurations for AWS, Azure, GCP, and Vault are validated for required fields when you create them through the API. Before this release, you might successfully configure secret storage only to have it fail during a secret operation.


## 5. Job history queries get faster


On large installations, the job history queries have made the UI crawl. To speed up these queries, Airbyte 2.2 does the following:


- Adds indexing on` jobs(created_at)` and on the commands workload lookup
- Gives job pruning and connection-timeline event pruning a ten-minute statement timeout
- Rewrites attempt statistics to use bound array parameters and chunked queries


You'll notice the cost for this update during the upgrade. Those indexes are created concurrently outside a transaction. For this reason, you can expect a large` jobs` table to sit in that step for a long time during startup. Plan your maintenance window accordingly rather than assuming the pod is wedged.


One more thing in the same spirit: a failed schema discovery on the refreshed-catalog path no longer blocks the connection page from loading, so you can actually reach the connection and fix the source of the problem instead of being locked out.


## Housekeeping notes before you upgrade


This upgrade is one-way. The 2.2.0 migrations drop tables that 2.1.x depends on, so a database that has run the migration can't serve 2.1.x images, and nothing dropped is recoverable. Take a backup.


Then, in order:


1. Grep` values.yaml` for` global.jobs.resources` and` global.workloads.resources.replication.*` . Confirm the values are what you want or remove them.
2. Find every API caller using` curl -u` and switch it to an access token. You can get this token by following the steps in[Airbyte documentation](https://docs.airbyte.com/platform/using-airbyte/configuring-api-access) .
3. If you mirror or pin bundled images, mirror manifest-server tag` 7.23.7` . Pods won't start without it.
4. Schedule enough of a window for concurrent index creation on your` jobs` table.


Find the full details in the[2.2 release notes](https://docs.airbyte.com/release_notes/self-managed/v-2.2) .
